references.text: [ref:Jes 40:3|Isaiah 40:3] is the prophecy that John the Baptist quotes in response to the question of who he is – "a voice crying out in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord".

In [ref:5 Mos 18:15-18|Deuteronomy 18:15–18], Moses promises that the Lord will raise up a prophet like him. The envoys from the Pharisees wanted to know if John was this prophet and therefore demanded that he explain who he was.

[ref:Mal 4:5|Malachi 4:5] prophesies that Elijah will be sent before the great day of the Lord. This expectation is the background for why the envoys ask John about his identity – they wanted to know if he was the promised Elijah.
[ref:Luk 3:15|Luke 3:15] tells us that the people wondered in their hearts whether John might be the Messiah. This uncertainty reflects the urgent question in John 1:22 regarding his identity.

[ref:Matt 3:1-3|Matthew 3:1–3] describes the ministry of John the Baptist and identifies him as the one Isaiah prophesied about – the voice crying out in the wilderness. This is the synoptic parallel to the answer John gives to the question in John 1:22.
[ref:Joh 1:23|John 1:23] is the direct answer John gives to the question in verse 22. He identifies himself as "a voice crying out in the wilderness," referencing Isaiah 40:3.
In [ref:Joh 5:33-35|John 5:33–35], Jesus refers to John the Baptist as the one who testified to the truth – a testimony closely linked to the question of John's identity and mission.
